verdict.rationale: Keycloak is documented as a self-managed server: it runs from a container image via `docker run`, installs on Kubernetes or OpenShift through the Operator, clusters through a caching layer, and sits behind your own reverse proxy. Its docs tell you to switch to a production database such as PostgreSQL, and user data can stay in your own LDAP/AD or other stores via federation or custom providers. Community reports corroborate long-running self-hosted deployments in the cloud, on-prem and in Windows enterprise environments. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the full set of supported external databases and their configuration (only the PostgreSQL pointer is evidenced).
